answer: Every new account must be introduced by three established operators who each lock a ninety-day surety of fifty stable-units. If the newcomer is later proven to be a clone, those sureties are slashed in full and the sponsors lose introduction rights for a season. At the zenith of a growth campaign, a farm of n fake agents therefore costs 150n units of locked capital plus frozen privileges. Even near a participation nadir the same posted price applies, so throwaway keys never become cheap votes. Sponsors publish lock receipts at a public jetty of settlement checkpoints that auditors can replay.
